title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints needed to reproduce the run, (ii) diagnose—using archived artifacts—why the paired outcome is uninformative about independent generative reliability (preregistered shared_initial_candidate design, template‑tight task synthesis, and validator–task coupling), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity, and expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while producing informative independent comparisons. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Automating NetOps by translating human intent into device configuration is operationally valuable but correctness‑critical: generated commands must preserve reachability, ACL invariants, and transient safety during multi‑step changes. Deterministic verifiers that compute the semantic effects of configurations (reachability, ACL equivalence, transient invariants) are established pre‑deployment tools; combining LLM generation with verifier grounding is therefore a promising evaluation pattern. To produce reproducible, auditable inference we preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 (SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). The preregistered primary question (H1) asked whether a single‑pass LLM generation pipeline has a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline on N = 120 intent→configuration tasks. The confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on per‑task binary verifier outcomes. We froze seeds, generation semantics, validator, scoring rules, and stopping rules before model calls were made and archived all execution artifacts.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation and intent→configuration research. Offline semantic validators (Batfish family and related work) demonstrably reduce deployment risk by checking reachability, isolation, and forwarding before push [Moore et al.; Batfish lessons: https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps studies explore intent translation and generate–validate–repair loops and highlight that text‑level fluency correlates poorly with operational correctness; verifier grounding is necessary for trustworthy automation [examples in the artifact record]. Our work differs by preregistering a paired statistical estimand and by releasing a byte‑level artifact manifest (responses, provider traces, validator JSONs, and all SHA‑256 fingerprints) to permit exact reruns and targeted reruns that change only the generation semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and high‑level design. The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) specified a paired confirmatory design (paired_binary_analysis_v1), N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class), generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one canonical candidate per pair presented identically to both conditions), and the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as scoring oracle. All frozen fields, seeds, retry policy, and stopping rules are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json). The declared model is gpt‑5‑mini; the recorded model configuration file is execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous pipeline is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Task corpus and templates. Tasks were programmatically synthesized by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (version 5.0). Each task manifest entry (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) contains: initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence (ordered primitive changes that satisfy intent safely), workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty annotation (changed_interface_count, transient_rule_count). Representative manifest entries and seeds for tasks 000001–000006 are archived and were used as confirmatory examples in the run (see artifact_examples in the bundled evidence). Templates intentionally encoded operational safety constraints (e.g., make‑before‑break uplink switchover; atomic paired MTU change) so the validator checks correspond to concrete operational properties.

Generation semantics, adapter, and execution accounting. The hosted adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the provider adapter 'openai_responses' was used to call gpt‑5‑mini. The preregistered confirmatory generation semantics 'shared_initial_candidate' produced one canonical candidate per task (shared_initial). That canonical candidate was reused for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; stored shared candidates are available under execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt (example SHA‑256s: task‑000001 shared candidate SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...). Execution accounting: planned_episode_count = 240 (120 pairs × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial generation counted once per pair); failed_episode_count = 0. Full provider call traces and call_cache artifacts are archived under execution/provider_calls and execution/call_cache. The exhaustive per‑file SHA‑256 manifest is included in execution/execution_manifest.json to enable byte‑for‑byte reproduction.

Deterministic validator and scoring rules. We used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) to parse generated commands, normalize configuration sequences, enforce task workflow_policies, check transient safety invariants (e.g., maintain minimum_active_in_groups during change), and compute final_state reachability and ACL invariants. The per‑episode scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation (binary: VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 when all required_commands and transient constraints were satisfied). Each scoring episode emitted a structured JSON trace archived in execution/scoring/*.json (representative file: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). The JSON traces include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validator_id, validator_version, and detailed violation lists when present.
sections.results:
Confirmatory aggregated counts and inference. All confirmatory episodes completed without infrastructure failures (complete_pair_count = 120). The archived counts are: baseline_success_count = 120/120 (baseline pass rate = 1.00) and guarded_success_count = 120/120 (gpt‑5‑mini pass rate = 1.00). The paired contingency table is degenerate: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 9f25790c7e...). The paired estimator (mean over tasks of guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. Following the frozen analysis plan (paired_binary_analysis_v1) we computed a 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) on the paired difference; the CI is [0.00, 0.00]. The exact McNemar two‑sided test yields p = 1.0. All analysis artifacts (condition_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg) are archived under analysis/ with SHA‑256s for verification.

Representative episode traces. The scoring JSONs provide full validator diagnostics. For task‑000001 the guarded scoring JSON (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...) records: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, normalized_configuration equal to the canonical shared candidate, final_state matching the required expected_final_state, and violation_count = 0. The canonical shared candidate file (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be...) shows the exact command sequence evaluated by both conditions. Similar identicalities between baseline, guarded, and shared_initial files occur across many pairs (several triplets share identical SHA‑256 fingerprints; see execution/responses/*.txt in the manifest). These traces demonstrate that the same artifact was scored under both conditions, producing identical pass outcomes.

Contamination checks and provider traces. Preregistered contamination heuristics (exact match and normalized n‑gram overlap thresholds) ran and recorded no confirmed contamination flags under the chosen thresholds; the results are in analysis/contamination_summary.csv. Full provider call traces and call_cache entries are archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/call_cache/*.json) so external auditors can reapply alternate exposure heuristics if desired.
sections.discussion:
Why the confirmatory paired test is uninformative for independent generative reliability. The artifact evidence shows that, by design, the shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical canonical candidates per pair that were scored in both conditions by the same deterministic validator. When identical artifacts are evaluated under a deterministic oracle, their pass/fail outcomes must match; therefore the paired test measures cross‑condition validator consistency on identical inputs rather than the independent per‑condition generative reliability that practitioners care about. The observed degenerate contingency table (n_11 = 120) correctly reflects that design choice and the validator's determinism.

Operational interpretation and artifact‑grounded remedies. For deployment questions—"How often will independently drawn LLM candidates satisfy verifier constraints?"—the appropriate confirmatory design is independent_per_condition sampling (generate one independent candidate per condition per pair) or a multi‑seed confirmatory design (K ≥ 3 independent samples per condition) to estimate per‑condition pass probabilities. The current artifact bundle enables exact reruns: reconfigure the generation semantics to independent_per_condition or produce additional seeds (the generator and seed logic are archived) and reexecute the validation harness. Because all provider traces, response files, validator JSONs, and the exhaustive SHA‑256 manifest are published, such reruns preserve deterministic reproducibility while answering the independent sampling question.

Threats to validity and limitations (artifact‑anchored). Internal validity: the preregistered shared_initial design intentionally removes generation variability and thus cannot detect model stochastic failure modes; construct validity: the deterministic validator faithfully enforces template constraints but may overestimate operational correctness on template‑aligned intents; external validity: the study used a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic templated tasks limiting generalizability; conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency table yields a trivial paired estimate—correct but not informative about independent generative reliability. All these limitations are documented with artifact traces (execution/scoring/*.json, execution/responses/*) and in the archived preregistration.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released a complete artifact bundle enabling byte‑level reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the declared LLM pipeline validated on all N = 120 tasks (120/120 each). Archived evidence (shared_initial candidate files and validator scoring traces) shows that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate paired outcome; consequently the confirmatory paired result does not provide evidence about independent LLM generative reliability in operational settings. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory execution, validator diversification, and expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while producing informative independent comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments. Transparent preregistration plus exhaustive artifact publication clarifies precisely what a confirmatory test measures and accelerates corrective reruns that answer the operational questions NetOps practitioners require for deployment decisions.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
